The game scared me, scared me to know that people do this in real life, and at points I was so into the story that I felt like I was actually spying on people. 
I don't know whether choices matter in this game, some parts (especially the ending) seemed to suggest so, if it does that would make the game better, if not, I believe that should be in there - this would work great as a choices matter. The ending did confuse me, which also suggested that choices matter, but I require further playthrough before doing so.

Overall, this is a good game, and I would recommend if you like a very story-driven experience!

game_name: Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You
review_text_raw:
Pros:
- The game brings awareness to important social problems: surveillance and totalitarianism
- Music is OK
- The characters are relatable
- Story is realistic
- This implementation of mass surveillance is plausible


Cons:
- Lack of depth in decision. The game is basically linear, except the ending which is a binary moral choice. No replay value.
- Lack of immersion stemming from weak game mechanics.
- The conflict system makes no sense and works against realisticity. How in the world can the system predict that something is in conflict with an unknown data chunk? A conflict should only be shown when both data chunks are known. 
- Phone calls wait for you to tap, such as everything in this game. No time pressure or feeling of urgency.
- The web is way too small, and computer hacking is way too minimalistic to be plausible.
- The enjoyment as you progress is almost a total downward slope. I think the last episode and the ending is just not ready.
- Game lasts no more than 8 hours.

game_name: Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You
review_text_raw:
I played through this game on Origin and recently received the game through steam via a Humble Monthly Bundle; so I felt it was time to put my thoughts on the game out there. I'm someone who is very aware of the constant privacy invasions of our internet connected lives, and how we are losing ground constantly. One of my favorite books is 1984 by George Orwell, so the name of this game was the first thing to pique my interest before I knew what it was about. Without any major spoilers, you play as an employee of a Big Brother-like watch system over the people in your country at the beginning of its implementation. You spend the game looking at a computer OS style UI where you scan through documents, web pages, and other online material to profile people for this "all-seeing" system. 
     
     The most interesting thing about this game is how well it presents all the different types of dangers (as well as pros if you look for them) with surveillance systems like the United States NSA stuff that has come out over the past years. It does such a good job at it because you aren't just looking at leaked documents about the system, but you ARE the system. Which means you make mistakes (or not) which leads to incorrect profiles and taking things out of context, which  endangers everyone. 

     Orwell is by far the best way to have someone that doesn't understand why national surveillance is bad for its citizens, truly understand all the intricacies and nuances of such a complex issue. I highly reccomend everyone play through this game. I honestly wish everyone had to play through this game so that misinformation and ignorance surrounding this issue would be minimized and we could all work together for the benefit of society as a whole. Play this game, and get someone else to play it; you won't be disappointed!

This game looks like what my wife sits on her phone every day doing. Just scrolling through a bunch of random crap. And it's just about as boring as that looks too.

From what little I played, I just opened some news articles. I was told to move highlighted text over to the "Orwell" aka the left side of the screen. Wow, what a thrilling game. I'm glad I don't have a desk job or this might feel like work.

Then I got yelled at for moving something over. Okay, my bad, I was just trying to be a good mover-over.

Next I clicked on some more junk, moved it over without reprimand.  Then I unlocked the "listener" cuz I tapped into some account or something. Yay me! I'm totally a government spy now!

And then that's it. Nothing happened after that. I ran out of stuff to click on, ran out of highlighted stuff to move. So I just waited for something to maybe happen, like record a conversation through my tap. But nothing ever happened, and if I really am supposed to just sit around and wait for a convo to happen, then good lordy, this is the worst game ever.

If I just didn't know what to do, then good lordy, it's still a pretty boring game that I have no interest in.

But hey, if you like clicking on words, then buy this. You won't regret it...unless you get stuck at the part I did, which was like 3 minutes into the game...
